# Results manifest: what each file is and how to read a method name

All numbers are computed by `scripts/02_run.py` (experiments, raw predictions in `results/raw/*.pkl`, not committed) and `scripts/03_analyze.py` (tables below). Scores are fractions in [0,1]; multiply by 100 for points. Every row says its benchmark, split and n (items); N is in `per_bench.csv`.

## Method names: `<design>|<estimator group>`
Design (how the n items are chosen, from source models only): `uniform` (SRS), `strat` (items sorted by source difficulty, one random item per stratum of N/n), `pps` (inclusion prob. ∝ √(p̂(1−p̂)) mixed with ε uniform, systematic PPS in difficulty order; ε chosen on sources), `balanced` (greedy forward selection from a random pool of 4n items so the subset mean matches the sources' full scores), `anchor` (k-means with n clusters on item response vectors, medoid per cluster, weight=cluster size), `infotop` (top-n items by 2PL information; deterministic), `cat` (adaptive max-information item selection per target with the d=1 2PL; no draw randomness).
Estimator group (from the n answers of the target): `mean` (Hájek weighted mean), `calreg` (OLS of sources' full score on their subset score), `irt-model` / `knn-model` / `ridge-model` (mean over all N items of the predicted outcomes; the predictor is fitted on sources and the target's n answers: `irt` = logistic latent-factor model, d=2, MAP ability; `knn` = k nearest sources by agreement on the sample, `ridge` = linear kernel ridge from sample responses to the full response vector), `*-plugin` (observed answers on the sample + model prediction on the unsampled items), `diff-irt|knn|ridge` (difference estimator: model mean over all items + λ × weighted mean of the 5-fold cross-fitted residuals on the sample), `diffnaive-irt` (same with non-cross-fitted residuals at λ=1; diagnostic), `fixed:<name>` (hyper-parameters fixed to λ=1; diagnostic of the cross-fitting bias).
Hyper-parameters (ε, k, ridge α, λ) are picked per (benchmark, split fold, n, design, group) on an inner split of the *sources* (see PROTOCOL.md); the pickled records keep the choice (`chosen`) and its inner RMSE.

## Files (results/)
- `audit.csv` — per benchmark: N, models kept after dedup, dropped duplicates, score range, families (Table 1).
- `targets.csv` — per (benchmark, split): k targets, number of independent families, thin flag (<10 targets or <5 families).
- `per_bench.csv` — per (bench, split, n, method): `rmse` (sqrt of mean over targets and draws of squared error), `mae`, `bias` (mean signed error), `bias2` (mean over targets of squared draw-mean error), `var` (mean over targets of draw variance, ddof=1; 0 for the deterministic designs), `ratio` = rmse / rmse of `uniform|mean`, `thin`.
- `primary.csv` (n=100) and `ratio_by_n.csv` — geometric mean over benchmarks of `ratio` per (split, n, method) with 95 % family-bootstrap interval (2000 replicates; families resampled within each benchmark; flavour `non_thin` excludes thin cells, `all` includes them); `n_bench` benchmarks entering. Benchmarks are not independent (HELM models recur across its benchmarks; OLL families recur across OLL benchmarks): the interval reflects target-family sampling only.
- `ordering.csv` — Spearman, Kendall τ-b, top-decile precision and top-decile Kendall per (bench, split, n, method); computed per (fold, draw) over that fold's targets, then averaged.
- `pairwise.csv` — pairwise order accuracy by bin of the true score gap (|gap| bins in score points: 0–0.5, 0.5–1, 1–2, 2–4, 4–8, >8 as `gap_bin` 0..5) and `ref_acc`, the sample-only reference: probability that n uniformly sampled items order a pair correctly given only that pair's own answers, Φ(|gap|/sd) with sd² = (disagreement − gap²)(1−n/N)/n computed from the pair's full vectors.  ## 0. The paper in one paragraph
 Evaluating an LLM on a full benchmark is costly, so we run it on n ≪ N items and predict its full score. Existing methods (anchor points, tinyBenchmarks, metabench, assessor, active acquisition) use the score matrix of *source models* to pick items and fit a *latent model* of the target; they are judged mostly on held-out models that resemble the sources. We cast the problem as **finite-population estimation of a mean of N unknown 0/1 values with a free covariate (the source matrix)**. That frame separates what the sources can buy — **variance reduction** — from what must be controlled by design — **bias**. We (i) test, on 13 binary matrices and under three target splits (interpolation, extrapolation, lineage-held-out), whether model-based predictors lose accuracy where targets differ from the sources; (ii) test whether a design-based correction (probability sampling with a positivity floor + difference/GREG estimator) repairs it and at what variance cost; (iii) measure how much the source matrix can help at all over plain stratified/balanced random sampling; (iv) examine ordering of models separately from score error. A negative or conditional answer to any of these is a result.
